title: Exact four-uniformity under Koo--Kwon condition (42)
summary: Determine whether the Koo--Kwon finite-field binomials have differential uniformity exactly four throughout every branch of condition (42).

formal_statement.body: Let $q=p^n>523$ be an odd prime power with $q\equiv3\pmod 4$, let $r=(q+1)/4$, and let $\chi$ be the quadratic character of $\mathbb F_q$. For $u\in\mathbb F_q^*\setminus\{\pm1\}$, define $F_{r,u}(x)=x^r(1+u\chi(x))$ and $\delta(F_{r,u})=\max_{a\in\mathbb F_q^*,\,b\in\mathbb F_q}|\{x\in\mathbb F_q:F_{r,u}(x+a)-F_{r,u}(x)=b\}|$. Suppose either $\chi(1+u)=(-1)^r\chi(1-u)$, or $q\equiv3\pmod 8$, $p>3$, and $u\in\{\pm(1-2^{r+1})/3\}$. Must $\delta(F_{r,u})=4$ for every such $(q,u)$?

scope.domain: Differential uniformity of odd-characteristic finite-field binomials
assumptions: $q=p^n>523$ is an odd prime power with $q\equiv3\pmod 4$
$r=(q+1)/4$ and $\chi$ is the quadratic character of $\mathbb F_q$
The two exceptional-value branches additionally require $q\equiv3\pmod 8$ and $p>3$
scope.unresolved_remainder: The source proves $\delta(F_{r,u})\le4$ on the character and exceptional-value branches and verifies equality computationally for $523<q<10000$. Exact equality remains unproved for every admissible $q>523$ and $u$ in the character, positive exceptional, and negative exceptional branches.

citations.label: Koo--Kwon, condition-(42) exact four-uniformity conjecture
citations.locator: Section IV, experimental paragraph after Theorem 4.9 and condition (42), p. 26

progress.summary: The source extrapolates the observed equality to every admissible field order above 523 and explicitly notes that a rigorous proof is missing.
